message.content: READ-ONLY audit of the caliper repo (do not edit, commit, push or open PRs; write only /tmp/claude-501/audit-shared-state.md). Use `git fetch origin` and read from origin/main (`git show origin/main:<path>` or a checkout of it in your own worktree). Context: the Entire reviewer and our own audits keep finding SHARED-STATE defects: results that depend on which consumer touched a cache first, or on timing. Recent real cases: (1) one oxc_resolver cache shared by the dependency loader and the resolution context made a tsconfig check pass wrongly (oxc caches a tsconfig reached via `references` without its own references), then the fix primed the cache in the other direction; the base design (separate unprimed caches) was the only sound one and was proven by a differential test over layouts x orders; (2) a test counter that was a process-wide static; (3) memos that were 'completed-only' so concurrent identical work started twice (convert memo, declared symbols), fixed with single-flight (`asked.rs` Answers/BatchAnswers, `Flights` with a cycle check); (4) kept-answer read recording (`kept.rs` Reads) must see every file the checker read, including during `updateSnapshot` reroots; (5) non-determinism: heap-meter wrap-around degraded some runs, checker-internal symbol ids leaked into names (`__#8@#type`), timeout fallback depends on wall clock. TASK: inventory EVERY piece of shared or long-lived mutable state across crates/core, crates/semantic, crates/binding, crates/cli: memos/caches (`Mutex<FxHashMap`, DashMap/FxDashMap, OnceLock/OnceCell/`Answers`, `Arc<..>` caches, `static`/thread_local/lazy statics, the DTS cache `cache.rs`, `dependency_types` Loader memos, resolver `Memo`, `ResolutionContext` caches, `State` in semantic convert.rs, `kept.rs`, `lazy.rs` revision engine, `on_demand.rs`, `watch`, NAPI sessions). For EACH: owner, who reads/writes it (threads/tasks/sessions), lifetime (per call/per load/per revision/per snapshot/per process), key (is the key a complete description of what the value depends on? e.g. depth/enclosing/options/tsconfig/condition names/listing), whether it is single-flight or completed-only, how it is invalidated on edit (watch/lazy/on-demand: mtime+size, revision, snapshot release), whether its value can differ by consumer or by the ORDER consumers touch it (give a concrete order that would change a result), and whether a test pins the order-independence. Flag: (a) keys that omit an input the value depends on; (b) caches shared across consumers with different options; (c) values cached that depend on timing, load or heap (the heap budget and timeout fallbacks: which components fall back, and is the output deterministic given the same input on a loaded machine?); (d) state reachable from both the batch `extract` and the long-lived session paths with different invalidation; (e) statics/thread-locals in non-test code; (f) any cache whose failure/degrade path stores a degraded value that later consumers read as authoritative (a fallback result cached as if it were the answer); (g) checker snapshot lifecycle leaks (a snapshot made and not released on an error path). Rank by 'would produce a wrong or non-reproducible output', then 'wasted work', then 'memory'. For each hit: file:line, the concrete failing order or interleaving, severity, minimal fix and the test that would prove it (a model-based differential test where the oracle is separate state per consumer). Then a section 'MODEL AND ARCHITECTURE CHANGES': e.g. a documented ownership map (docs/architecture) of every shared state with its key, lifetime and invalidation; one `Memo`/`Answers` abstraction with single-flight, key type and invalidation hook so ad hoc maps are not written; a rule that determinism is a tested property (`gate_harness determinism` under load, loom/shuttle-style interleaving tests for the cycle check in `Flights`), making degraded results carry a marker so they are never cached or compared; with cost and what each would have prevented among the five cases. Be concrete; top 10 hits first. Final message: max 200 words with the path, counts per severity and the top 3 changes. Cap 90 tool calls; never ask questions.

227	/// TypeScript's own generic utility types — never prop providers, and expanding
228	/// them structurally needs a type checker we don't have. `Omit`/`Pick`/`Partial`/
229	/// `Readonly` get real structural handling as alias shapes (see resolver/alias.rs);
230	/// this list exists so every OTHER arity/usage of these names (and the ones with
231	/// no structural handling at all) degrades to a silent no-op instead of a
232	/// spurious "cannot resolve" warning. Shared by chain.rs (props level) and
233	/// named.rs (type level) — previously duplicated as two independently-maintained
234	/// name lists that happened to agree, with no guard against them drifting apart.
235	pub(super) fn is_ts_utility_type(name: &str) -> bool {
236	    matches!(
237	        name,
238	        "Omit"
239	            | "Pick"
240	            | "Partial"
241	            | "Required"
242	            | "Readonly"
243	            | "NonNullable"
244	            | "ReturnType"
245	            | "Parameters"
246	            | "Awaited"
247	            | "Extract"
248	            | "Exclude"
249	            | "Record"
250	            | "ReadonlyArray"
251	            | "Array"
252	            | "Promise"
253	    )
254	}

256	// ─── ResolutionContext ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
257	
258	/// Shared, read-only context passed to all resolution functions.
259	/// Arc'd so it can be cheaply shared across rayon threads.
260	pub struct ResolutionContext {
261	    pub global: Arc<GlobalSourceData>,
262	    pub import_map: Arc<ImportResolutionMap>,
263	    /// Fast `(file, name)` index over `global.interfaces`/`type_aliases` and
264	    /// their declared generic type parameters — see `named_type_index.rs`'s
265	    /// module doc for why this exists alongside (not instead of) those flat
266	    /// maps.
267	    pub(crate) named_types: Arc<crate::named_type_index::NamedTypeIndex>,
268	    pub oxc_resolver: Arc<Resolver>,
269	    /// `ModuleResolvers::types_first`.
270	    pub(crate) types_first_resolver: Arc<Resolver>,
271	    /// Module resolutions by `(directory, specifier)`. Resolution only reads the file system, which a run treats as
272	    /// fixed, and every component importing from the same directory asks again; a watch revision builds a fresh
273	    /// context, so nothing outlives one revision.
274	    pub(crate) module_resolutions:
275	        dashmap::DashMap<(Box<str>, Box<str>), import::ModuleResolution, rustc_hash::FxBuildHasher>,
276	    /// React's declaration file by importing directory, cached as `module_resolutions` is.
277	    pub(crate) react_types_files: dashmap::DashMap<Box<str>, String, rustc_hash::FxBuildHasher>,

18	/// The id of a cycle-set key, the same for every state in the process. The keys are `file:name<arguments>` strings tens
19	/// of bytes long; the sets and the read logs of the interface-chain recordings (`resolver::memo`) hold ids instead,
20	/// so copying a set or a log copies numbers, and no reference count is shared between the threads resolving components.
21	/// Ids are never reused, so equal ids are equal keys.
22	fn key_id(key: &str) -> u32 {
23	    static IDS: std::sync::OnceLock<dashmap::DashMap<Box<str>, u32, rustc_hash::FxBuildHasher>> =
24	        std::sync::OnceLock::new();
25	    static NEXT: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32::new(0);
26	    let ids = IDS.get_or_init(Default::default);
27	    if let Some(id) = ids.get(key) {
28	        return *id;
29	    }
30	    *ids.entry(key.into()).or_insert_with(|| NEXT.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed))
31	}

41	    /// `visited` above. `visited` is chain.rs's, permanent for the rest of a
42	    /// given branch's resolution (with per-sibling-branch cloning to avoid
43	    /// diamond-inheritance false positives — see `resolve_interface_chain`).

45	    /// unrelated field's type across a whole component, not once per
46	    /// interface, so a permanent set would falsely flag two different,
47	    /// non-cyclic fields that happen to share a type (`{ a: Shared; b: Shared
48	    /// }`) as circular. This set instead tracks only what's currently on the
49	    /// live call stack — inserted on entry to `resolve_named`, removed before
